name: brainrot (brain rot)
blurb: Low-value, endlessly scrollable content, and the foggy feeling of consuming too much of it
title: Brainrot Meaning: What Does Brainrot Mean in Slang?
description: Brainrot is slang for low-value, absurd online content and the fog of bingeing it. Thoreau coined it in 1854; Oxford made it Word of the Year 2024.
answer: Brainrot (or brain rot) means two linked things: low-quality, often absurd online content that you keep scrolling anyway, and the dulled, foggy state it supposedly leaves you in. Kids also use it as a label for a whole style of nonsense humour, as in "that video is pure brainrot". The phrase goes back to Henry David Thoreau's Walden in 1854, and Oxford University Press named brain rot its Word of the Year on 2 December 2024, after usage rose 230% from 2023 to 2024.

body: In the first sense brainrot is a complaint: hours of short videos, recycled jokes and AI slop that feel like they are melting your attention span. People say "I have brainrot" after a doomscrolling night, half joking and half worried.

In the second sense it is a genre. Teens call a meme brainrot when it is loud, repetitive and funny because it makes no sense, from Skibidi Toilet to the 2025 wave of AI-generated Italian brainrot characters. Here the word is closer to an affectionate tag than an insult, and people who speak in a stream of these references are said to talk in brainrot.

body: After Oxford's pick the word moved from teen slang into news stories, school talks and parenting advice about screen time. Among young people it is still everyday vocabulary for nonsense memes. It is a figure of speech, not a medical diagnosis, though it reflects real worries about attention and heavy short-video use.

faq.q: Is brainrot one word or two?
faq.a: Both are used. Oxford's Word of the Year is written brain rot; online, especially for the meme genre, it is usually brainrot.

faq.q: Who first used the term brain rot?
faq.a: Henry David Thoreau, in Walden (1854). He used it about a decline in thinking, not about the internet.
A 2025 meme wave of AI-generated characters with Italian-sounding names and text-to-speech voices, such as Tung Tung Tung Sahur. It took its name from the brainrot genre.
